- Small dark brown/black spots at lower left with yellowing around them
- A small lesion near top that appears to have dropped out (shot-hole appearance)

**Analysis of test image:**
- Soybean leaf on dark soil
- One lesion at upper area where tissue has fallen out (shot-hole appearance)
- 2-3 small dark brown/black rounded spots at lower-left with distinct yellow halos
- Leaf is otherwise mostly green

**Key comparisons:**
- **Frogeye_leaf_spot**: Circular-to-angular dark spots with reddish-brown borders, shot-hole where centers fall away, yellow halo possible — matches well (reference top-right panel closely resembles test image)
- **Bacterial_Blight**: Angular water-soaked spots with yellow-green halos — the reference shows many more spots and more angular/vein-bounded lesions than the test image
- **Phyllosticta_leaf_spot**: Gray/tan lesions with dark margins and shot-holes — lesions appear tan/gray, not dark brown as in test image
- **Septoria_brown_spot**: Heavier spotting with rapid yellowing from bottom canopy — doesn't match

The combination of discrete dark rounded spots, yellow halos, and the shot-hole appearance (tissue center falling out) is most characteristic of **Frogeye_leaf_spot**. The frogeye reference images show this exact pattern — scattered dark circular spots on green leaves with shot-holes — matching the test image closely.
